  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING

  THURSDAY, NOVEMBER 13, 2025
  6:00 PM

 1)  CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Dean Henderson called the meeting to order at 6:00 pm.

 2)  ROLL CALL

  Present: Chair Dean Henderson, Vice Chair Getro Elize, Commissioners David Lujan,
  Mateo Olivarez, Ayeasha Jones
  Absent: None

 3)  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Commissioner David Lujan led the Pledge of Allegiance.

 4)  CONSENT CALENDAR - Now is the time for public participation.

  4.1)  Waive full reading of the Resolution(s) to be considered and voted on at this
  meeting. (This allows for reading the title only in lieu of reciting the entire text).

  4.2)  Approve the Planning Commission meeting minutes of October 9, 2025.

  Motion: Approve all items listed on the Consent Calendar.
  Moved by David Lujan, seconded by Getro Elize.

  Vote: Motion carried (5-0)
  Yes: Chair Henderson, Vice Chair Elize, Commissioners Lujan, Olivarez, Jones

5)  PUBLIC HEARING - Now is the time for public participation. Each public hearing will
  have its own public testimony.

  5.1)  Adopt Resolution No. PC-2025-009, a Resolution of the Planning Commission of
  the City of Palmdale, California, approving Major Modification 24-0024, a request
  to expand and reconfigure the existing Antelope Valley Recycling And Disposal
  Facility from 185 Acres to 351 acres, located at 1200 City Ranch Road, and finding
  that the Addendum prepared for the project is consistent with the previously
  Certified Environmental Impact Report.
   Clerk Magallanes read the resolution into the record.

  Chantal Powers, Contract Planner, presented the item and noted that she and the
  applicant were available to answer questions.

  Chair Henderson opened the public hearing.

  Public testimony in support was heard from the following individuals: David Harris of the
  Community Development Center USA, Michelle Santian of Girl Scout Troop #5971, Mr.
  Perry of Social Vocational Services for Disabled Adults, Steve Arklin of Antelope Valley
  Landfill, and Kevin Bailey, a local resident.

  Jayna Morgan, on behalf of the applicant, addressed the commission and introduced the
  team involved in the project.

  Commissioners and staff discussed concerns about the project, including noise and odor
  mitigation, which will be included as conditions of approval to reduce their impact as
  trucks arrive and depart the landfill, ensuring compliance with state regulations.

  Felicia Trong, Chief Environmental Health Specialist at the Department of Public
  Health’s Local Enforcement Agency, addressed the Commissioners as the point of
  contact for any landfill-related concerns.

  Chair Henderson closed the public hearing.

  Motion: Adopt Resolution No. PC-2025-009, as amended.
  Moved by Ayeasha Jones, seconded by David Lujan.

  Vote: Motion carried (5-0)
  Yes: Chair Henderson, Vice Chair Elize, Commissioners Lujan, Olivarez, Jones

6)  NON-AGENDA PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Public Testimony: None.

7)  STAFF COMMUNICATIONS

  Megan Taggart, Director of Economic and Community Development, announced the Pines
  and Presents community event at the Auto Mall, starting November 28, 2025. In addition, Jolly

8)  COMMISSIONER REPORTS, ANNOUNCEMENTS

  Ayeasha Jones announced a community event at Kensington Center in Lancaster from 9 am

  Chair Henderson adjourned the Planning Commission meeting at 6:54 pm to Thursday,
  December 11, 2025, at 6:00 pm in the City Hall Council Chamber located at 38300 Sierra
  Highway, Suite B, Palmdale, California.

  PASSED, APPROVED, and ADOPTED this 12th February 2026.

  Dean Henderson, Chair

  RECOMMENDATION

  Staff recommends that the Planning Commission:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. PC-2026-001, a Resolution of the Planning Commission of
  the City of Palmdale approving Major Modification (MOD) 25-0026 and Time
  Extension (TE) 26-0002, and find that the project is categorically exempt from
  environmental review.

  BACKGROUND

  The application for the MOD was submitted on June 23, 2025, reviewed by staff, and
  deemed incomplete on July 8, 2025. After the resolution of completeness items, the
  application was deemed complete on December 22, 2025. Subsequently, a TE
  application was submitted on January 20, 2026, to extend the facility's operation for
  another 10 years. This application was also deemed complete and scheduled for the
  Planning Commission meeting on February 12, 2026.

  The original project was approved by the Planning Commission under Conditional Use
  Permit (CUP) 08-16 (Resolution No. PC-2008-055) on October 16, 2008. The approval
  authorized a 55-foot-high major wireless telecommunication facility within an associated

and was approved by the Planning Commission on June 13, 2019, extending the

ANALYSIS

The proposed project is Major Modification 25-0026 and Time Extension 26-0002,
requesting the demolition of an existing major wireless telecommunications facility and
existing mechanical equipment, constructing a new 56-foot monopole tower, installing
new mechanical equipment within an existing 240 square-foot equipment enclosure, and
granting a 10-year extension of time for the continued operation of the facility. The project
site is in the Heavy Industrial (HI) zone, which permits major wireless telecommunications
facilities with review and approval of a CUP, as outlined in Palmdale Municipal Code
(PMC) Table 17.65.020-1 (Allowed Uses - Industrial Zones). The site currently operates
under an active CUP 08-16TE No. 1, which expires on July 8, 2029. Because the project
involves a substantial modification to the existing major wireless telecommunications
facility and a time extension for the continued operation of the facility, it requires review
and approval of a MOD and TE, as specified in PMC Sections 17.95.010.B (Definitions),
17.20.100.B (Modifications to Land Use Approvals), and 17.95.040 (Operational
Standards - Time Limits).

Site Layout

  FIGURE 2 - SITE PLAN

Access

Access to the project site will continue to be provided via the paved access road off 6th
Street East, adjacent to the existing towing facility on the property. Access to the
telecommunication facility will be needed only for routine maintenance and will utilize the
existing on-site parking.

Architecture

The proposed project involves the construction of a light gray monopole
telecommunications tower. Its cylindrical monopole design supports panel and rail-
mounted antennas clustered near the top, reaching an overall height of approximately 56
 Staff Report to Planning Commission
MOD 25-0026 and TE 26-0002
February 12, 2026
Page 9

feet above ground level. The light gray finish is intended to minimize visual contrast and
blend with the sky. The monopole is supported by a concrete foundation and surrounded
at the base by an existing six-foot-tall concrete masonry unit (CMU) wall that screens
ground-mounted equipment. The arm-mounted antenna arrangement and minimal
ground-level improvements create a clean, unobtrusive appearance suitable for the
surrounding area, as shown in Figure 3.

  FIGURE 3 - NORTH ELEVATION

ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW

The proposed project is categorically exempt from review under the California
Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines pursuant to Section 15302 (Class 2 -
Replacement or Reconstruction) of the CEQA Guidelines, which exempts the
replacement or reconstruction of existing structures and facilities where the new structure
will be located on the same site as the structure replaced and will have substantially the
same purpose and capacity as the structure replaced. The proposed project involves
demolishing an existing major wireless telecommunications facility and existing
mechanical equipment, constructing a new 56-foot monopole tower, installing new
mechanical equipment within an existing 240 square-foot equipment enclosure, and
granting a 10-year extension of time for the continued operation of the facility. The project
does not propose any expansion of the site.

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF
  PALMDALE, APPROVING MAJOR MODIFICATION 25-0026 AND
  TIME EXTENSION 26-0002; A REQUEST TO DEMOLISH AN EXISTING
  MAJOR WIRELESS TELECOMMUNICATIONS FACILITY AND EXISTING
  MECHANICAL EQUIPMENT, CONSTRUCT A NEW 56-FOOT MONOPOLE
  TOWER, INSTALL NEW MECHANICAL EQUIPMENT WITHIN AN
  EXISTING 240 SQUARE-FOOT EQUIPMENT ENCLOSURE, AND GRANT
  A 10-YEAR EXTENSION OF TIME FOR THE CONTINUED OPERATION OF
  THE FACILITY, LOCATED AT 37822 6TH STREET EAST, AND FINDING
  THAT THE PROJECT IS CATEGORICALLY EXEMPT FROM
  ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW

  WHEREAS, SBA Communications Corporation has filed an application
requesting the approval of Major Modification (MOD) 25-0026 and Time Extension (TE)
26-0002, described herein (hereinafter referred to as “Application”); and,

  WHEREAS, the Application applies to a parcel located at 37822 6th Street East,
as indicated on the Los Angeles County Assessor roll as Assessor Parcel Number
3010-023-006, legally described on Exhibit A hereto and shown on the map attached
hereto as Exhibit B; and,

  WHEREAS, on February 12, 2026, the Planning Commission of the City of
Palmdale conducted a duly noticed public hearing on the Application and concluded said
hearing on that date.

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE CITY
OF PALMDALE DOES HEREBY FIND, DETERMINE, RESOLVE, AND ORDER AS
FOLLOWS:

  SECTION 1. The Planning Commission hereby specifically finds that all the facts
set forth in the Recitals of this Resolution are true and correct.

  SECTION 2. The Planning Commission hereby finds as follows with respect to the
environmental document prepared for this project:

  A  The project is categorically exempt from environmental proceedings
  pursuant to Section 15302, (Class 2 - Replacement or Reconstruction), of
  the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines, which
  exempts the replacement or reconstruction of existing structures and
  facilities where the new structure will be located on the same site as the
  structure replaced and will have substantially the same purpose and
  capacity as the structure replaced. The proposed project involves
  demolishing an existing major wireless telecommunications facility and
 Resolution No. PC-2026-001

  existing mechanical equipment, constructing a new 56-foot monopole
  tower, installing new mechanical equipment within an existing 240 square-
  foot equipment enclosure, and granting a 10-year extension of time for the
  continued operation of the facility. No expansion to the site footprint is
  proposed.

  B  The custodian of records for all other materials which constitute the record
  of proceedings upon which the Planning Commission’s decision is based,
  is the Planning Manager of the City of Palmdale. These documents are
  available for public review in the Planning Division of the City of Palmdale,
  located at 38250 Sierra Highway, Palmdale, California 93550, telephone
  (661) 267-5200.

  SECTION 3. Based upon substantial evidence presented to this Commission
during the above-referenced February 12, 2026, public hearing, including public
testimony, and written and oral staff report, this Commission specifically finds as follows:

  A  The proposed use is consistent with the goals, policies, and objectives of
  the General Plan. (CUP) (MOD)

  B  The proposed use is beneficial and desirous to the community and is
  consistent with the purpose, intent and standards of this Title and other
  applicable ordinances and codes adopted by the City. (CUP)(MOD)

  The project is consistent with the policies and objectives outlined in the
  General Plan and the Development Standard Table shown in Exhibits C and
  D. The site is located within the Industrial (IND) General Plan land use
  designation and the Heavy Industrial (HI) zone. The project is a request to
  demolish an existing major wireless telecommunications facility and existing
  mechanical equipment, construct a new 56-foot monopole tower, install new
  mechanical equipment within an existing 240 square-foot equipment
  enclosure, and grant a 10-year extension of time for the continued operation
  of the facility. The site currently has an active CUP approval, CUP 08-16TE
  No. 1 (Resolution No. PC-2019-022), approved by the Planning
  Commission on June 13, 2019. This use is permitted under Palmdale
  Municipal Code (PMC) Table 17.65.020-1 (Allowed Uses - Industrial
  Zones). As the project involves a substantial modification to the existing
  major wireless telecommunication facility and an extension of time for the
  continued operation of the facility, the project requires review and approval
  of a MOD and TE, as specified in PMC Sections 17.95.010.B (Definitions),
  17.20.100.B (Modifications to Land Use Approvals), and 17.95.040
  (Operational Standards - Time Limits). As described in Exhibit D
  (PMC Standards), the project complies with the specific development
  standards, setback, and height standards. Furthermore, the proposed
  project features a light gray monopole telecommunications tower. Its
 Resolution No. PC-2026-001
MOD 25-0026 and TE 26-0002
Page 3

  cylindrical monopole design supports panel and rail-mounted antennas
  clustered near the top, reaching an overall height of approximately 56 feet
  above grade. The light gray finish is intended to minimize visual contrast
  and blend with the sky. The monopole is supported by a concrete foundation
  and surrounded at the base by an existing six-foot-tall concrete masonry
  unit (CMU) wall that screens ground equipment, providing for a smooth
  transition to the surrounding industrial area.

  C  The proposed use and the ongoing operation of the use will not have a
  substantial adverse effect on abutting property or the allowed use thereof,
  and will not generate excessive noise, vibration, traffic, or other
  disturbances, nuisances, or hazards. (CUP) (MOD)

  The proposed major wireless telecommunication facility will serve as a low-
  impact, low-traffic use, as access to the telecommunication facility will only
  be needed during construction and routine maintenance. It will ensure the
  continued provision of reliable and efficient wireless network service to
  nearby areas without the need to construct a new facility in undeveloped
  areas, and is consistent with the General Plan as shown in Exhibit C.

  D  The site for the proposed use has adequate pedestrian and vehicular
  access. (CUP) (MOD)

  Access to the project site will continue to be provided via the paved access
  road from 6th Street East, which is located adjacent to the existing towing
  facility on the property. Access to the telecommunication facility will be
  needed only for routine maintenance and will utilize the existing on-site
  parking. In addition, the project has been reviewed by the Los Angeles
  County Fire Department and Engineering Division, and it has been
  determined to have adequate access to ensure safe vehicular and
  pedestrian flow.

  SECTION 4. Based on the findings and conclusions set forth in Sections 1, 2, and
3 above, this Commission hereby approves MOD 25-0026 and TE 26-0002 subject to
the Conditions of Approval as set forth in Exhibit E.
